column12: Judgement on the comparator, house convention. Stivarga (regorafenib) is the STELLAR-303 control arm, the oral VEGFR multikinase inhibitor zanzalintinib replaces in third-line mCRC, and the only drug in this line in the book's demand table (Fruzaqla and Lonsurf are not carried). The engine bills each start as at least one patient-year, so a per-beneficiary spend is the right kind of figure for a short course. The case against: a Stivarga beneficiary's spend reflects regorafenib's short time on drug (median PFS 2.0 months in the STELLAR-303 control arm), while zanzalintinib's is 3.7 months, so this understates spend per zanzalintinib patient. Stivarga's beneficiaries also include GIST and HCC use. Cabometyx, Exelixis's own oral TKI, reads $132,512 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Cabometyx), but that is mostly long-duration first-line RCC, not this setting. Atezolizumab is billed by Roche under Part B and is not Exelixis revenue

column12: The sought label is metastatic CRC previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin- and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, and an anti-EGFR if RAS wild-type (CancerNetwork on the NDA acceptance), the same third-line population as the regorafenib, trifluridine/tipiracil and fruquintinib labels. Cross-check: Takeda puts US third-line and later mCRC at 14,600 patients (HUTCHMED filing, as returned by search, not opened), which counts fourth-line patients again. Case for a larger pool: dMMR is rarer by third line than in first-line trials, because most dMMR patients now get immunotherapy first and many respond durably. Case for a smaller one: 28.8% of post-chemotherapy pMMR patients get best supportive care only (Desai et al., below), and Nevala-Plagemann counts only those treated

column12: Judgement: 1.0x regorafenib's measured capture, the incumbent zanzalintinib beat head to head on overall survival (HR 0.80). The denominator is treated patients, the same basis as Nevala-Plagemann's third-line count in eligible_pct. Case for higher: the first immunotherapy-based regimen with an OS gain in non-MSI-H mCRC, sold by a company already calling on these oncologists with Cabometyx; a new entrant in this line can grow fast (Fruzaqla in-market sales $290.6mm in 2024 and $366.2mm in 2025, HUTCHMED 20-F FY2025 0001104659-26-023822, as returned by search, not opened); and a drug used in fourth line also reaches patients counted once here. Case for lower: the 2016-2021 data predate trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab and fruquintinib (both 2023), so the line now splits more ways; grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 60% vs 37% on regorafenib; the co-primary endpoint in patients without liver metastases missed at the final analysis (HR 0.83, p=0.1185, Q2 2026 10-Q); and IV atezolizumab every 3 weeks adds infusion visits to an otherwise oral line
